claim.why_it_matters: Within one clause the transcription puts some subclause headings at markdown level 2 and their own siblings at level 3, so an outline or TOC built from the file shows 9.1.7.3 and 9.1.7.4 as peers of 9.1.7 rather than children of it, and 9.1.8.1 as a peer of 9.1.8. Heading text, number and anchor are all correct, so no normative content is lost; this is navigational only. The defect correlates exactly with page-slice boundaries (every heading inside the page-250 slice was emitted at '##'), so it is a systemic scaffolding artifact, not a per-page transcription error.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED as a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. (1) Nothing is missing, so the 'missing-heading' kind is factually wrong. I rendered page 250 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v250/spec_p250.png, printed page number 220) and read every glyph: the page carries exactly four headings -- '9.1.7.3  Relative', '9.1.7.4  Indexed', '9.1.8  Access modes', '9.1.8.1  General' -- and specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 11118, 11129, 11140, 11143 carry all four with byte-identical heading text, correct clause numbers, and correct anchors (section-9-1-7-3, section-9-1-7-4, section-9-1-8, section-9-1-8-1) matching the TOC links at lines 391-394. All four bodies of prose on the page are also present and complete. (2) The only difference is the markdown '#' count, which is pure formatting and carries no content. The hierarchy is fully and unambiguously encoded in the heading text itself ('9.1.7.3' is self-evidently a child of '9.1.7'), so nothing about the document's meaning or structure is recoverable-only-from-the-lost-signal. (3) There is no counterpart signal in the PDF to be unfaithful to: on the rendered page, '9.1.7.3 Relative', '9.1.7.4 Indexed', '9.1.8 Access modes' and '9.1.8.1 General' are all set in the SAME bold face at the SAME point size with the same left margin and the same numbering-to-title tab. ISO does not vary heading typography by depth here, so the markdown cannot be said to have dropped a distinction the source drew. The claim's own premise that the PDF marks 9.1.7.3/.4 as fourth-level and 9.1.8 as third-level is an inference from the clause number, not an observation of the printed page -- and that clause number is exactly what the transcription preserved. (4) The claim's causal theory is falsified. It asserts the defect 'correlates exactly with page-slice boundaries'. The very next slice refutes that: inside the page-251 slice, line 11180 emits '### 9.1.9 Reel and unit', where 9.1.9 is a third-level peer of 9.1.7, 9.1.8 and 9.1.10 (line 11192 correctly emits '## 9.1.10 Current volume pointer'). That is a depth error in the OPPOSITE direction inside a slice whose other headings (9.1.8.2/.3/.4) are correct, so 'every heading in a slice was flattened to ##' does not describe the mechanism. (5) Note for the record: an internal inconsistency in the markdown's own heading-depth convention does exist and is worth a mechanical cleanup -- normalize '#' depth from the dot-count of the clause number across the whole file, which would fix 9.1.7.3, 9.1.7.4, 9.1.8.1 and 9.1.9 in one pass. But that is an intra-markdown style nit, not a discrepancy between the PDF and its transcription, and it belongs in a global normalizer rather than the per-page reconciliation ledger.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-to-markdown discrepancy. All four page-250 headings (9.1.7.3 Relative, 9.1.7.4 Indexed, 9.1.8 Access modes, 9.1.8.1 General) are present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md with correct text, clause numbers, anchors and body prose; nothing is missing. The sole difference is the markdown '#' depth, and the PDF itself prints all four headings in identical bold type at identical size, so no source distinction was lost. What is genuinely true -- and is a separate, file-wide style issue rather than a page-250 transcription error -- is that heading depth is not consistently derived from the clause number's dot-count: 9.1.7.3, 9.1.7.4 and 9.1.8.1 are emitted one level too shallow ('##'), while on the following page 9.1.9 Reel and unit is emitted one level too deep ('###') even though it is a peer of the '##' 9.1.10. Fix, if desired, with a single global pass that sets heading depth from the clause number, not with a page-250 edit.
